result:
The proposed solution has an error in the coefficient $a_4$, and the final answer is too large.

**Where the error is.** Expanding $1+\frac{zf''}{f'}=1+2a_2z+(6a_3-4a_2^2)z^2+(12a_4-18a_2a_3+8a_2^3)z^3+\dots$ and matching against $e^{\omega(z)}$ gives
$$a_4=\frac{c_3}{12}+\frac{5}{24}c_1c_2+\frac{17}{144}c_1^3,$$
not $\frac{13}{72}c_1c_2+\frac{11}{144}c_1^3$.

A quick check: for $\omega(z)=z$, $\frac{zf''}{f'}=e^z-1$ gives $f'=\exp\!\big(z+\tfrac{z^2}{4}+\tfrac{z^3}{18}+\dots\big)=1+z+\tfrac34z^2+\tfrac{17}{36}z^3+\dots$, so $a_4=\tfrac{17}{144}$, which agrees with my formula and not with the proposed one.

**Corrected expression.** Recomputing $\Gamma_3=-\frac{c_3}{24}+\frac{1}{16}c_1c_2-\frac{5}{288}c_1^3$ and then
$$\Gamma_1\Gamma_3-\Gamma_2^2=\frac{c_1c_3}{96}-\frac{c_2^2}{144}-\frac{c_1^2c_2}{192}+\frac{c_1^4}{2304}.$$
The $\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2$ formulas and the $a_2,a_3$ relations in the proposal are correct.

**Upper bound.** Use the Schur parametrization with $r=|c_1|$, $s=1-r^2$, $|c_2|=st$, and $|c_3|\le s(1-t^2)+rst^2$. Taking absolute values of every term gives
$$|\Gamma_1\Gamma_3-\Gamma_2^2|\le \frac{rs(1-t^2)}{96}+\frac{r^2st^2}{96}+\frac{s^2t^2}{144}+\frac{r^2st}{192}+\frac{r^4}{2304}.$$
The right side is increasing in $t$, so $t=1$ is the worst case. With $u=r^2$, it becomes $\frac{16+4u-19u^2}{2304}$, whose maximum over $u\in[0,1]$ is at $u=\frac{2}{19}$ and equals
$$\frac{308/19}{2304}=\frac{77}{10944}.$$
So the supremum is at most $\frac{77}{10944}\approx 0.00704$, while the proposed answer is $\frac{77}{9792}\approx 0.00786$. The proposed value is therefore too large. (The structure of the proposed computation is right; the mistake is the $17/144 \to 11/144$ slip, which changes $19$ into $17$ in the final numerator.)

I did not pin down the exact supremum, but the bound above rules out $77/9792$.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 4
